subject: Best way to control "eval" behavior of set of chunks

messages.author: 5f171faf83bd9c08
messages.subject: Best way to control "eval" behavior of set of chunks
parts:
I have been running large simulations in code chunks and the results
are used elsewhere in the document.

Because they generate so much data, I don't even want to cache them.
Rather, what I am doing is putting in a "save(...)" at the end of
these chunks which would dump the results into a Rdata file for
reference. Another file I save is a summary data file which I save to
a different Rdata file to be read-in for plotting parts of the
document.

What I would like to do is set "eval=FALSE" to these (memory hogging)
simulation chunks easily.
There are multiple number of these chunks, so changing them to TRUE
when I want to run them is a big pain.

So, when I am ready to rebuild the document from scratch including the
simulations, I can change one thing and run it overnight.

Is there something I can do which would selectively set eval=TRUE or
eval=FALSE for predetermined set of chunks?

Thanks!

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Best way to control "eval" behavior of set of chunks
parts:
How about setting all other chunks explicitly to eval=TRUE, and leaving eval unspecified for the chunks you want to toggle.  Then you could toggle the global option eval=FALSE to eval=TRUE when you wanted evaluate those chunks?  (I believe local options always over-ride global).  Otherwise I'd just try adding a common pattern in your chunk-name that was easy to run find/replace on.

just a thought.
Carl

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Best way to control "eval" behavior of set of chunks
parts:
Did you read section 3.5 of the manual?
https://github.com/downloads/yihui/knitr/knitr-manual.pdf

This is one major difference between knitr and Sweave -- for knitr,
your Rnw document is programmable (via chunk options).
